earlier_scan.source_named: Ancient language known only from Libyco-Berber inscriptions; OLAC/Glottolog list no grammar or phonology; no stress description can exist for the epigraphic corpus.

sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes the Libyco-Berber script is an abjad without vowels; word comparisons add vowels by normalization from modern Berber.

sources.citation: Chaker, Salem. 2008. Libyque : ecriture et langue. Encyclopedie berbere 28-29: 4395-4409. https://journals.openedition.org/encyclopedieberbere/344
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Para 17: 'Le libyque est un alphabet consonantique, principe eminemment semitique, plutot mal adapte au berbere.' Para 27: interpretation is hazardous because vowels, fundamental in Berber, are not written. No mention of accent/prosodie.

sources.citation: Chaker, Salem. 2002. L'ecriture libyco-berbere. Etat des lieux, dechiffrement et perspectives linguistiques et sociolinguistiques. Colloque annuel de la SHESL, Lyon-ENS, 2 fevrier 2002, 12 pp. (author's PDF; precursor text of the Encyclopedie berbere entry 'Libyque : ecriture et langue', EB 28-29, 2008)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. States the script is purely consonantal ('le libyque est un alphabet consonantique', p.4; 'l'ecriture ne representant pas les voyelles', p.8) and that phonological knowledge is limited to a structurally coherent picture of the consonant system (p.7).

sources.citation: Chaker, Salem. 1986 [1988]. A propos de la terminologie libyque des titres et fonctions. Annali dell'Istituto Universitario Orientale di Napoli 46/4: 541-562 (author's re-issue PDF)
sources.note: Lexical/etymological study of Libyque titles; vocalizations are reconstructed from modern Berber; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Roessler, Otto. 1958. Die Sprache Numidiens. In: Sybaris. Festschrift Hans Krahe zum 60. Geburtstag, 94-120. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The fullest linguistic analysis of Numidian (consonant system, morphology) cited by Galand and Chaker; would confirm first-hand that nothing beyond consonants is recoverable. Cannot contain a stress rule.

sources.citation: Kerr, Robert M. 2010. Some thoughts on the origins of the Libyco-Berber alphabet. In H. Stroomer et al. (eds), Etudes berberes V, 41-68. Koeln: Koeppe.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Recent treatment of the script and its phonetic values (incl. final H possibly marking a vowel); would not contain a stress statement but is the modern reference on what the script encodes.

sources.citation: Galand, Lionel. 1973. L'alphabet libyque de Dougga. Revue de l'Occident musulman et de la Mediterranee 13-14: 361-368. doi:10.3406/remmm.1973.1216
